strings.d1.s0.name: Palace of the Grand Master
strings.d1.s0.tips: The knights' 14th-century palace (restored by Mussolini), with mosaics from Kos. Part of the UNESCO-listed Old Town.
strings.d1.s1.name: Street of the Knights
strings.d1.s1.tips: Ippoton Street, lined with the inns of the seven languages (France, Spain and others) and stone arches.
strings.d1.s2.name: Sokratous Street & Suleymaniye Mosque
strings.d1.s2.tips: The Ottoman bazaar street from the Turkish period (1522-1912), with the mosque and a Turkish library.
strings.d1.s3.name: Mandraki Harbour Deer
strings.d1.s3.tips: The deer columns stand where the Colossus of Rhodes is said to have been. Take in the windmills and the Fort of St Nicholas.
strings.d1.s4.name: Nireas Rhodes Old Town
strings.d1.s4.tips: A taverna under a vine canopy, serving octopus. It sits near the Jewish Quarter (Evreon Martyron).
strings.d1.b0.name: Marco Polo Café
strings.d1.b0.tips: A garden in an Ottoman mansion, also open in the evening.
strings.d1.b1.name: Old Town Walls
strings.d1.b1.tips: Guided walks along the top of the walls run on set days. Walking the moat is free.
strings.d2.s0.name: Lindos Acropolis
strings.d2.s0.tips: Take the bus (1.5 hours, leave at 08:00) or drive. See the Temple of Athena Lindia and views over St Paul's Bay. Go when it opens at 08:00, as midday reaches 40°C, and walk rather than ride a donkey.
strings.d2.s1.name: Lindos Village
strings.d2.s1.tips: White captains' houses with pebble-mosaic courtyards, narrow lanes and the Church of Panagia.
strings.d2.s2.name: St Paul's Bay
strings.d2.s2.tips: The bay is calm in winter, though swimming takes some courage.
strings.d2.s3.name: Mavrikos Lindos
strings.d2.s3.tips: A square-side taverna since 1933, serving seafood and listed in the Michelin guide.
strings.d2.s4.name: Lindos Main Beach
strings.d2.s4.tips: A winter beach walk with the acropolis lit up above.
strings.d2.b0.name: Captain's House Lindos
strings.d2.b0.tips: A bar in a captain's house in Lindos.
strings.d2.b1.name: Pefkos Beach
strings.d2.b1.tips: A quiet beach south of Lindos.
strings.d3.s0.name: Kallithea Springs
strings.d3.s0.tips: A 1929 Italian Art Deco spa with mosaic courtyards. Swim and snorkel in the cove.
strings.d3.s1.name: Anthony Quinn Bay
strings.d3.s1.tips: The cove from the Greek film Zorba. Turquoise water, pebbles and rock, empty in the morning, with sunbeds.
strings.d3.s2.name: Faliraki Beach
strings.d3.s2.tips: A long sandy beach with beach tavernas, good for lunch.
strings.d3.s3.name: Tsambika Beach
strings.d3.s3.tips: Golden sand and shallow water. The monastery on the hill is up 300 steps and comes with a fertility legend.
strings.d3.s4.name: Tsambika Monastery Sunset
strings.d3.s4.tips: A hilltop monastery with a panorama of the coast.
strings.d3.b0.name: Ladiko Beach
strings.d3.b0.tips: Anthony Quinn's neighbouring cove, and quieter.
strings.d3.b1.name: Stegna Beach Taverna
strings.d4.s0.name: Symi Ferry Mandraki
strings.d4.s0.tips: The Dodecanese high-speed ferry takes 1 hour (return about 30 EUR) and arrives at Yialos harbour.
strings.d4.s1.name: Yialos Harbour Symi
strings.d4.s1.tips: Pastel neoclassical houses rise like an amphitheatre around what is often called Greece's most beautiful harbour.
strings.d4.s2.name: Kali Strata Stairs & Chorio
strings.d4.s2.tips: 500 steps up to the old town, with a castle and views. It is cooler in the morning.
strings.d4.s3.name: Symi Shrimp at Manos Fish
strings.d4.s3.tips: Small fried Symi shrimp, eaten shell and all, by the harbour.
strings.d4.s4.name: Panormitis Monastery
strings.d4.s4.tips: The monastery of the Archangel Michael, where the ferry calls. It is the holiest in the Dodecanese. Return between 16:00 and 17:00.
strings.d4.b0.name: Nos Beach Symi
strings.d4.b0.tips: A small beach beside the harbour, an alternative to the monastery (depending on the ferry route).
strings.d4.b1.name: Tholos Symi
strings.d4.b1.tips: A seafront taverna at the end of the harbour.
strings.d5.s0.name: Valley of the Butterflies Petaloudes
strings.d5.s0.tips: There are no butterflies in winter, but you get a green stream walk and waterfalls.
strings.d5.s1.name: Ancient Kamiros
strings.d5.s1.tips: The Hellenistic "Pompeii of Rhodes", with a sea-view agora and a cistern.
strings.d5.s2.name: Kritinia Castle
strings.d5.s2.tips: The ruins of a knights' castle, with free views over the Aegean.
strings.d5.s3.name: Kritinia Village Taverna
strings.d5.s3.tips: On the village square: goat and pitaroudia (chickpea fritters).
strings.d5.s4.name: Embona Wine Village
strings.d5.s4.tips: Wine tasting at the foot of Mount Attavyros (Emery, Alexandris) in a mountain village.
strings.d5.b0.name: Monastery of Filerimos
strings.d5.b0.tips: On Ialysos hill, with a Calvary path, a giant cross and peacocks. An alternative to Kamiros.
strings.d5.b1.name: Emery Winery Embona
strings.d6.s0.name: Prasonisi
strings.d6.s0.tips: It becomes an island in winter when the water rises. Expect windswept views.
strings.d6.s1.name: Prasonisi Taverna Lighthouse
strings.d6.s1.tips: The only cluster of tavernas on the sand spit, serving fish.
strings.d6.s2.name: Kiotari Beach
strings.d6.s2.tips: A long, quiet beach on the way back.
strings.d6.s3.name: Asklipio Castle & Village
strings.d6.s3.tips: Byzantine church frescoes and a castle in an inland village.
strings.d6.s4.name: Gennadi Beach Sunset
strings.d6.s4.tips: An empty pebble beach. The drive back takes 1.5 hours.
strings.d6.b0.name: Kiotari Taverna Paraga
strings.d6.b0.tips: On the beach, an alternative to Prasonisi.
strings.d6.b1.name: Monolithos Castle
strings.d6.b1.tips: A castle on a rock on the west coast with sunset views. An alternative route.
strings.d7.s0.name: Elli Beach Morning
strings.d7.s0.tips: The city beach, with a diving platform and the Turkish coast in view.
strings.d7.s1.name: Rhodes Aquarium
strings.d7.s1.tips: An Italian aquarium from the 1930s, out on the headland.
strings.d7.s2.name: Nea Agora Mandraki Breakfast
strings.d7.s2.tips: The round courtyard of the New Market, for coffee and loukoumades (honey doughnuts).
strings.d7.s3.name: Rhodes Airport Bus
strings.d7.s3.tips: The bus to Diagoras Airport takes 30 minutes. Time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Koskinou Village
strings.d7.b0.tips: A village of colourful doors, an alternative to the aquarium.
strings.d7.b1.name: Ronda Beach Bar Elli
strings.note0: A hire car is essential (Lindos, Prasonisi, the west). KTEL buses run regularly along the east coast (Lindos takes 1.5 hours). The airport bus costs 3 EUR.
strings.note1: From November to March it is 12-18°C, most beach facilities and Lindos tavernas are closed, and the Old Town and villages are quiet. April-May and October are ideal (sea at 22°C).
strings.note2: The palace costs 12 EUR (April-October), the Lindos acropolis 12 and the Symi ferry 30. A taverna meal runs 20-30. For tips, round up the bill.
strings.note3: The ferry from Marmaris takes 1 hour (Schengen visa needed for Turkish citizens). There is also a summer ferry from Fethiye.
strings.note4: Try pitaroudia, melekouni (sesame and honey bar), souma (grape spirit) and Symi shrimp, plus Embona wines.
strings.note5: Pickpockets are rare in the Old Town. Motor vehicles cannot enter, so you will need to walk with your luggage.
